title: A Scalable and Robust Compilation Framework for Emitter-Photonic Graph State
problem: Generating quantum graph states is critical for distributed quantum computing and quantum algorithms, but existing compilation approaches for deterministic emitter-photonic schemes lack scalability for larger graphs and ignore hardware characteristics, resulting in impractical high-overhead implementations.
motivation: Deterministic emitter-photonic graph state generation is more scalable than probabilistic photonic schemes, but compilation remains a bottleneck with no existing framework optimizing for both scalability and hardware constraints.
method: A hierarchical compilation framework that partitions large target graph states into smaller subgraphs, compiles each independently, then combines and schedules circuits to maximize emitter resource utilization. Incorporates local complementation to transform graph states and minimize entanglement overhead during recombination.
key_novelty: Graph partitioning with local complementation transforms and hierarchical scheduling for emitter-photonic implementations, tailored to hardware constraints.
contributions: Graph partitioning algorithm decomposing quantum states into compilable subgraphs
Local complementation-based graph transformation minimizing entanglement overhead
Emitter resource utilization-aware scheduling for heterogeneous quantum hardware
52% reduction in CNOT gates and 56% reduction in circuit duration, plus 1.9× suppression of photon loss
baselines: prior photonic graph state compilation methods
limitations: Evaluation on selected graph types; scalability to fault-tolerant quantum error correction codes and large-scale distributed systems not discussed.
primary_theme: scalable quantum graph state compilation via partitioning and local complementation
